about: A predicted and a matched finding of the solve of the public corpus photo rp-b-01 (.cache/real-photos, data/downloads.json) on main 217982b9, each titled by a designation (the third too long to say whole with its class words at the old fit) while its catalog reference's common-name field holds its catalog id, as the upload path served them, for voice-star-name-1.

findings.title: Tau1 Eridani
findings.subtitle: Predicted Star (Eri) · 1 Eri · Gaia DR3 5129338021224785408 · 14.3 pc · Alt +24.1° Az 260.5° · Above Horizon

evidence.verificationMethod: Predicted for the given time and place; not measured in the image
evidence.distanceUncertaintyNote: Distance interval [14.2, 14.3] pc: the Bailer-Jones et al. (2021) photogeometric estimate from Gaia DR3, with its 16th to 84th percentiles
limitations: Predicted from its Gaia DR3 catalog row (epoch J2016.0), moved by its proper motion to the date, for the recorded capture time, its time zone taken from the GPS position and agreeing with the GPS time stamp, and place; not measured in the recording.
Its brightness is the catalog's own Gaia G magnitude, not the usual V.

Placed in the sky for that moment and place, at sea level; near the horizon it sits a little low, since the air's bending of light is left out. Its stated uncertainty adds UT1 - UTC (up to 13.5 arcseconds), polar motion, its own parallax (left out of its place), the stored precision of its motion, and, for a row with no proper motion or radial velocity, the motion it may have, up to the fastest star in the tiles; the catalog's own position and motion errors are not in it.

catalogRef.citation: Catalog id, Gaia G magnitude, color index (BP-RP) and radial velocity: Gaia DR3, Gaia Collaboration (2023) A&A 674, A1. Distance: Bailer-Jones et al. (2021) AJ 161, 147, photogeometric.

limitations: Distance is 1000/parallax from Hipparcos 2007, with the interval from the parallax error, not measured from this image.
Its brightness is the catalog's own Hipparcos Hp magnitude, not the usual V.
